entities.summary: Domenico della Rovere was an Italian cardinal and patron of the arts. He served as a diplomat for the Holy Roman Empire during the Italian Wars (1494-1559), negotiating with various European powers, including France and Spain. Della Rovere's artistic patronage supported prominent artists such as Raphael and Michelangelo. His diplomatic efforts led to the Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis (1559), which ended the Italian Wars and established a temporary peace in Europe. The cardinal's legacy extended beyond his own time, influencing the development of Catholicism during the Counter-Reformation. Della Rovere's diplomatic work also had a lasting impact on European politics, contributing to the rise of powerful monarchies and the decline of feudalism. In 1501, he died under mysterious circumstances in Rome, leaving behind a complex legacy that continues to fascinate historians today.
